notes: Example configuration generated by the CraneCalc configurator; fictitious crane, supplier, site and owner data, to be replaced with project data. Scope: 4 simply supported 45-ft bays, W36X487 girders, one 30-ton cab crane, on new freestanding W14X398 columns with column caps, base plates, anchor rods and spread footings, and crane-level rod X-bracing; the existing building carries no crane load. Seismic: ordinary steel cantilever column system across the runway and rod bracing not specifically detailed for seismic resistance along it, Seismic Design Category B. Bumper overhang assumed 20 in (end-wheel centerline to the extended bumper face, a typical supplier proportion): the stop contact positions use it; confirm with the crane supplier.

selections.designed: None: end fork on the column cap (bearing stiffeners and bolted bottom flange)
selections.reason: A girder on a column cap is held by its bearing stiffeners and bolted bottom flange (fork), the top-flange restraint of the analysis: no flange tie.

Lightest compact W within the sizing targets (ratio ≤ 0.85, deflections ≤ 0.9 of the limits): screening estimates, top-flange tip stress (DG7, warping and second-order twist) ratio 0.60, vertical deflection 0.29, lateral 0.78 and rail-head movement with twist 0.89 of their limits; flanges at least 10.5 in wide for the end bearing bolt gauge and the rail seat; lighter candidates rejected: 1 by deflection, 111 by sizing ratio, 63 by flange width; the next lighter, W36X441: rail-head movement with twist 1.02 of the limit > 0.9. These are the configurator's screening estimates (a simplified model that ranks the catalog), not the final ratios: the calculation checks the section and reports its own ratios.

New cantilever column for a 30-ton crane (W14X120 to 5 t, W14X159 to 12.5 t, W14X211 to 25 t, else W14X257). The W14X257 chosen for the crane gives base drift ratio 2.83 > 0.9: the lightest heavier W14 within the drift and torsion ratios; no rolled W14 to the W14X398 meets the new column's drift, torsion and twist ratios for this crane: an open item (New column beyond the W14 range).

selections.designed: Column cap with the girder end fork, kept
selections.reason: The column cap sized to the limits of its steps still exceeds bolt-slip 1.80 (sizing estimates; the calculation reports its own): the four 1 in A490 bearing bolts of each girder end take the fork couple at a 8.25 in gauge, and no larger bolt, grade or wider gauge the sizing tries lowers it within the nut clearances to the column flanges (a larger bolt's edge distance lengthens the bearings past the cap stiffeners' seat on the column flanges; a heavier W14 has about the same clear between its flanges). A fork for this crane needs the bolts spread wider (a column with a wider clear between its flanges, or bearing bolts on the cap beyond the column, designed by hand); the support entered is kept and checked (review draft: open item).

selections.designed: W14X398, closest; cap bearing bolts to be designed by hand
selections.reason: Column cap not resolved: sized to the limits of its steps it still exceeds bolt-slip 1.80 (sizing estimates; the calculation reports its own): the four 1 in A490 bearing bolts of each girder end take the fork couple at a 8.25 in gauge, and no larger bolt, grade or wider gauge within the nut clearances to the column flanges brings them within 1.00. Recommended: the fork couple on a wider bolt spread or more bolts (bearing bolts on the cap plate beyond the column flanges, or a column with a wider clear between its flanges), designed by hand. The closest cap is built and checked.

selections.designed: W14X398, closest; new column beyond the W14 range
selections.reason: New column beyond the W14 range: the heaviest rolled W14, W14X398, still gives base drift ratio 1.85 (configurator estimate; the calculation reports its own). The column would leave about 1.35 of the drift limit for the column alone, 1.84 with this footing's rotation (estimate): a larger footing is not enough. Recommended: a built-up or laced crane column, a deeper rolled W (W24 to W36, strong axis across the runway, designed by hand), or the column tops tied to a braced frame. The support entered is kept and checked.

fabrication.steel: Girder ASTM A992; plates, bars and stiffeners ASTM A572 Grade 50 unless noted.
fabrication.bolting: ASTM F3125 Grade A325, pretensioned, Class B faying surfaces, standard holes unless slots are detailed. Sliding-end bearing bolts and column-end tie bolts pretensioned against steel sleeves. Rail joints tight (gap 1/16 in max.), supplier's joint bars (deferred submittal) installed slip-critical: Class A surfaces, bolts pretensioned, re-tightened at 30 and 90 days.
fabrication.welding: E70XX low-hydrogen electrodes per AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020, cyclically loaded provisions. Continuous fillets as dimensioned; no intermittent welds on cyclic load paths. Smooth starts and stops.
fabrication.inspection: Visual inspection of all welds; AWS D1.1/D1.1M:2020 cyclically loaded acceptance criteria; magnetic particle testing of fillets at fatigue-sensitive attachments; 100% ultrasonic testing of CJP welds; bolt pretension verification per RCSC.
fabrication.erection: Set and level the bearings, install the end bearings and flange ties, then set the rails. Provide temporary restraint until the permanent ties are complete.
fabrication.railAlignment: Set the rails to the specified gauge, alignment and level tolerances and survey them after erection, before the load test.
